# G10 market notes for cross-market government bond spreads

Compact per-market differences that change how a cross-market spread should be built or read. Every item is dated
or cited; check current data before use.

## USD (Treasuries)
- Sets the tone for global back ends: "US rates do set the tone for global rates even in the face of large local shocks". Bunds and USTs move in near-identical directions; Bunds outperformed only in 2014-15; the ECB is a follower (Fed moved first at most turning points; ECB hikes and cuts by less, lower r*) (Willer and Saunders, Trading Global Macro Markets, 2026).
- Foreign share of Treasuries peaked near 57% after the GFC and was 32% at end-2025 (FT, Unhedged: Who owns government bonds?, Aug 2026). Foreign official demand tracks the USD and trade policy; private demand mixes fund inflows, basis trade and duration views vs carry (BofA, UST supply and demand in '25, Nov 2024).
- Policy support (a Treasury buyback signal at 30y 5.30%, about $16bn/quarter) may cap the belly and front end more than the back end; the signal's half-life was about one day (Citi, House Views, Aug 2026; FT, 20 Aug 2026).
- USD SOFR-ASW is the cleanest global rich/cheap yardstick (no capital-cost or term-risk component) (Huggins and Schaller, 2024).

## EUR (Bund, OAT, BTP, Bono, OLO, Dutch, Austrian, Finnish, Portuguese)
- Bund: less than one-tenth the size of USTs, highest 10y correlation with USTs outside Canada; relative safe haven with little room to rally if the ECB will not reverse (Citi, Global Resilience, 20 Aug 2026; Willer and Saunders 2026). Bund ASW vs EURIBOR/OIS embeds a capital-cost term (about g x q x d, 16bp at g 10%) and is more volatile than UST SOFR-ASW; basis swaps absorb much of the volatility (Huggins and Schaller 2024).
- Periphery yields have a monetary and a credit component; the spread is the credit part; a hawkish ECB raises funding costs and widens periphery spreads (Willer and Saunders 2026). BTP ASW traded in line with European credit (cheap above the BBB Z-spread, expensive near A/AA); sharp spikes can trigger ECB action.
- France (OAT): fiscal beta about 10bp per 1pt of GDP of 1y-ahead deficit expectations; 57% non-resident holdings at end-2025 and an implicit ECB backstop; 2027 presidential election risk premium; positive CDS-bond basis in the sovereign crisis because French bonds were hard to borrow (GS 2 Oct 2026; FT Aug 2026; Tuckman and Serrat 2022). In credit-stress regimes France trades as a hedging name for non-German EGB risk; invoice spreads widen and 2-10y euro-OIS becomes the only effective hedge (Astor Ridge, Trade Radar, Mar 2022). Hedge funds were about EUR50bn net long OAT repo with low haircuts (Barclays, 2 Oct 2026, citing a central-bank financial stability review).
- Italy: credit component dominates; repo reluctance turned the CDS-bond basis negative in 2009-12 and in the 2018 budget standoff (Tuckman and Serrat 2022). Redemption and coupon dates usually coincide with supply, so the auction cycle dominates (JPM, Follow the cash flow, Sep 2015).
- Netherlands: weak pre-auction concession, attributed to a pre-announced quarterly calendar (same JPM note). Austria: 3s10s screened too flat vs the spread level (JPM GFIMW, 21 Aug 2026). Rating-implied RV (e.g. Austria rich vs EU) failed repeatedly; supply and funding progress dominate (Citi, 1 Oct 2026).
- ECB tools: purchases follow capital keys with a one-third issue/issuer limit from 2015; PEPP dropped the limit, cut minimum maturity to 28 days and allowed flexibility on keys; supranational issuance (SURE, NGEU) sits outside the keys (Tuckman and Serrat 2022). Reaction-function ladder: verbal guidance and the policy rate first; balance sheet only for disorderly moves; TPI for unwarranted, disorderly spread moves, OMT as fallback; "ECB's pain threshold tends to be higher than that of markets" (BofA, Global Rates Weekly and Global Economic Weekly, 2 Oct 2026).
- Collective action clauses: EGBs with original maturity over 1y issued since 2013 carry CACs; the market does not price them differently, but newer bonds are more liquid and domestic-law bonds can have CACs retrofitted (Düring, 2021).
- SSA vs EGB: German agencies, German state issuers and Nordic agencies trade vs swaps (their spreads to EGBs widen when EGBs sell off vs swaps); French agencies and Belgian regions trade vs OATs and Belgian bonds. Funding completion and year-end balance sheet matter (Citi, European Rates Weekly, 24 Sep 2026).

## GBP (gilts)
- More sensitive to the UST long end and energy than Bunds; energy exposure can erode fiscal-rule headroom; BoE estimates the cumulative QT effect on the 10y at 20-30bp (Citi, Latest views, 20 Aug 2026). Domestic LDI/insurer buyers of long gilts are retreating, so the foreign share rises and the market becomes more price-sensitive (FT 2026).
- 1Yx1Y SONIA vs 1Yx1Y ESTR: beta 1.09, R2 95%; 5Yx5Y gilt vs UST beta 1.1, R2 75% (JPM GFIMW, Aug 2026): UK intermediate moves are mainly US-driven. Gilt-Bund four-factor checklist: macro, fiscal, BoE QT, seasonals (BofA, UK Rates Viewpoint, Sep 2024).
- Steepest SOFR-ASW curve among Bunds, USTs and gilts (BoE steep haircut schedule) (Huggins and Schaller 2024).
- Back-end US-UK spreads follow relative policy: in 2015-19 the spread peaked Nov 2018, one month before the last differential hike (Willer and Saunders 2026).

## JPY (JGBs)
- Domestic holder base (BoJ owned about 48% of JGBs: JWS Macro, Duration Is Diseased, Sep 2025); external factors move local ASW little; JGB USD ASW mirrors the JPY cross-currency basis and tracks Japan CDS (correlation 0.78, 2009-Jun 2012) (Huggins and Schaller 2024).
- Back end co-moves with USTs only weakly (weekly 10y correlation 0.28, against 0.79 for CAD; one source calls it high, trust the number) and has lower vol; front end lags the US front end and can be exploited; BoJ cycles are best positioned at the front end (Willer and Saunders 2026). The market converges with overseas curves, so overseas moves transmit more into Japan (Citi, Japan Rates Weekly, 14 Aug 2026).
- Hedged pickups: JPY investors saw negative hedged pickups to the home 10y/20y JGB through 2024-25, yet banks and some lifers kept buying; lifers hedge about half and pension funds treat hedged foreign bonds as domestic, so their foreign buying is mostly unhedged (BofA, FX-Sofr primer, Oct 2023; JPM, Cross currency basis 4Q24 Outlook, Sep 2024). Lifer net foreign-bond selling: JPY12.8trn (2022), 3.6trn (2023), 2.2trn to Oct 2024 (Citi, FX Basis Quarterly, Dec 2024).
- YCC breaks mechanical carry rules; MoF shifting issuance away from super-longs rather than buying back is "partially why 10s30s have been flattening since mid-2025" (Citi, House Views, Aug 2026). Citi used 1.5% as the yardstick for the US-Japan policy-rate spread (Citi, Japan Rates Weekly, 14 Aug 2026).

## CAD
- Highest correlation with the US (2y 0.59, 10y 0.79) (Willer and Saunders 2026); CAD/US is a neighbour pair (5y spread at a 1,000-day extreme tends to run about 2 more months before stabilising).
- CAD used as the vol-matched short against EUR 10y swaps (JPM, Rule-based Fixed Income, Nov 2012). The Canadian 10y screened rich in the global model in Apr 2025 (z -3.0) (BofA, Monthly rates models, 7 Apr 2025). CAD front end followed Fed rhetoric less in the last cycle (lower beta to the global central-bank factor) (JPM, Talk is Cheap, May 2024).

## AUD and NZD
- AUD/NZD is a neighbour pair with the best median reversal after a 1,000-day extreme on 5y spreads (about +-75 days, favourable skew) (Willer and Saunders 2026). AUD/NZD 5y5y vs USD: first PC explained 46% of the variance but R2 on USD changed from 0.47 to 0.76 around 2023 (Citi, Asia FX and Rates, 13 Aug 2026).
- FX-swap hedge references are term bank bills (3M BBSW, 90-day BKBM), not overnight rates, so match the hedge reference when comparing pickups; in global USD stress AUD/NZD bases can tighten while EUR/JPY widen (BofA, FX-Sofr primer, Oct 2023).
- Synthetic AUD bond via JGB + AUD/JPY basis swap (2015): 40bp pickup at 1y rising to about 120bp at 6-7y over ACGBs; MTM volatility from three legs (basis vol largest), so best at 1-2y or buy-and-hold (JPM, Drivers of cross currency basis, Mar 2015).
- Goldman Sachs expected AUD to outperform cross-market into the RBA terminal rate (market priced about 35bp of hikes over a year, the least in G10) (GS 2 Oct 2026). Japanese investors were net buyers of AUD government bonds in 6 of the last 8 Mays (BofA, bond seasonality, Jun 2022).

## CHF, SEK, NOK
- CHF benefits vs EUR from an OAT political risk premium (Citi, FX Forecasts, Aug 2026); the Swiss 10y screened rich in the global model (z -1.5 Apr 2025, -1.8 May 2025). SARON is secured, so CHF swap-vs-govt conventions differ from EUR OIS; see [fi-g10-market-conventions](../../fi-g10-market-conventions/SKILL.md).
- SEK and NOK are a neighbour pair: long 10y NOK vs SEK closed +20bp; pay 1y1y NOK vs SEK 147 -> 167bp closed +20bp (GS and Citi, Sep-Oct 2026). SEK 10y beta to USD 0.8, R2 56% over 1M (JPM GFIMW, Aug 2026). SEK was the highest-carry market (10y - 1m) in Mar 2017 and NOK second-lowest (JPM, rule-based update, Mar 2017). Small markets: use weekly data, widen cost assumptions.

## Seasonals (tailwind only)
Bond-market seasonal up-ratios on cross-market spreads (US-Bund up 70% in Feb and 30% in Aug; UK-Bund up 70% in Jan, Feb, Apr and 75% in Sep; CAD-US up 70% in Apr) rest on samples of 20 years (10 for Japan); global direction dominates local patterns and QE-era patterns may fade (BofA, Bond market seasonality explained, 6 Jun 2022). A 70% ratio on 10 observations is weak evidence. See [quant-seasonality-and-calendar-effects](../../quant-seasonality-and-calendar-effects/SKILL.md).
